issues.description: Predicate reads awkwardly; invert to express intent directly.
issues.detail: `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')` buries the rule. The data distinction is: a layer statement (no block) is allowed before @import; a layer with a block is not. Write `!(nodeName === 'layer' && node.nodes == null)` with a short comment, or extract `isLayerStatement(node)` so the algorithm follows the data shape.

PostCSS represents block-less at-rules with `nodes` absent and block-having ones with an array. `node.nodes == null` is shorter, conventional in this codebase, and matches the data shape directly. `typeof === 'undefined'` is defensive verbiage for a value PostCSS controls.

issues.description: Test coverage misses `@layer foo;` (statement form) regression case.
issues.detail: The new test covers the bug (layer with block), but no test asserts the still-allowed case: a block-less `@layer foo;` before `@import` must NOT report. Add one accept-case to lock the data distinction in place, so a future refactor of the predicate can't silently regress it.

review.summary: Small, correct fix. The data shape (layer-with-block vs. layer-statement) is the right distinction, and the algorithm follows from it once you see it. The predicate expresses the distinction in a roundabout way — a named helper or a clearer null-check would make the intent self-evident at the call site. Tests cover the bug but should also pin the allowed statement form so the data invariant is enforced both ways. Nothing structural to strip; this is right-sized.
